case_reviews.oracle: Enqueue leaves balance 100 and only the funding operation. A second maintained native Root drains the stored request, whose fields equal the original except the explicitly absent backpack-weight fact; balance becomes 90, frozen bytes stay identical, replay is Replayed(Ok) and six-table counts stay fixed.
case_reviews.limits: In-process Root reopen, not OS-process restart. SQL bootstrap seeds current custody. Count footprint is not complete row equality.

case_reviews.oracle: Independent connection, character-lease and scope generations are rejected with AuthorityRejected and zero confirmations. A valid enqueue succeeds; changed amount or NPC generation for the same command is ConflictingOccurrence. Runtime UPDATE frozen_request is SQLSTATE 42501; marking completion without an operation is deferred SQLSTATE 23514.
case_reviews.limits: Refusal coverage is three named generation fields and two binding changes, not every fence/source field. The two SQL privilege/proof cases use explicit fixture transactions.

case_reviews.oracle: A real deferred outbox trigger aborts the money transaction. Exact Unavailable, unchanged six-table counts and frozen bytes, balance 100, and completed=false precede trigger removal; retry then yields Some and balance 90.
case_reviews.limits: This is a distinct deferred commit failure, not five write-prefix crashes. Retry does not assert the full returned receipt; its state effect is independently observed.

case_reviews.oracle: Two maintained Roots run concurrently through join_two. Both return Some successful outcomes, exactly one is Committed, balance is 90, confirmation count is 1, and operations count is 2 including funding. BankOperationOutcome has only Committed and Replayed, so exactly one committed also establishes one replay.
case_reviews.limits: No equality assertion between the two returned BankOperationRecord values. No forced interleaving; the dedicated inflight case provides observed lock scheduling.

case_reviews.oracle: Before activation a native buy cannot spend bank balance. After explicit fixture activation, bank-only 25 and mixed 40 (10 coins plus 30 bank) produce exact balances 75/45, spent coin state and independent summary tuples. Decoded audit debit equals SQL entry and there is one item-audit event per transaction before replay. Replay is AlreadyCommitted, selected footprint and balance remain; insufficient 46 refuses.
case_reviews.limits: Direct native trade API with a privileged activation seed. Footprint omits game_npc_trades, game_npc_trade_lines and game_item_audit_outbox, so its replay snapshot does not itself verify those rows remain unchanged.

case_reviews.oracle: Native preview reads funded balance 100 and zero eligible coins; same-account and unresolved names yield distinct fixed refusals with no resolved recipient. Stale lease is AuthorityRejected and no confirmation is enqueued.
case_reviews.limits: No explicit other-World recipient is created in this body; it does not independently qualify the documented cross-World privacy branch.

case_reviews.oracle: A held native occurrence advisory lock causes Unavailable in under five seconds without count/frozen-byte/balance changes. After rollback, a second maintained Root commits the original and then replays with unchanged counts, balance 90.
case_reviews.limits: Upper timing bound and held lock qualify bounded refusal; there is no independent pg_blocking_pids observation or lower wait bound in this case.

case_reviews.oracle: A BEFORE INSERT trigger blocks the native writer on a fixture advisory lock; the isolated DB must expose at least one then two ungranted locks before release. Actual writer returns Committed(Ok), retained command returns Replayed(Ok), balance is 90 and operation count is 2.
case_reviews.limits: wait_for_blocked observes database-wide ungranted-lock counts, not exact backend identity or a specific lock edge. The fixture installs a scheduling trigger without disabling native transaction guards.

case_reviews.oracle: Literal 499-entry starting tree refuses buy/sell requests requiring overflow with DoesNotFit and unchanged selected counts/balance 200. A smaller buy commits to exactly 500 entries and balance 100.
case_reviews.limits: The large item tree is seeded with session_replication_role=replica; test execution restores ordinary role via transaction scope. Native mint/deposit funds money, but this tree construction bypasses ordinary item creation guards. This body relies on the common PG18 check rather than calling the exact-version helper itself.

case_reviews.oracle: Four replacement command kinds/payloads, each with transfer guard deferred or open, still invoke exactly one original command (ID 1 and exact session), invoke no step, emit exact accepted NPC result frames and advance next ID to 2.
case_reviews.limits: Historical outcome fixture supplies no current NPC, item fence or money authority; arbitrary replacement payloads are intentionally not accepted as new work.

case_reviews.oracle: An unknown retained result emits baseline only, invokes no replacement step, and leaves next ID at 1.
case_reviews.limits: No database or actual retained bank transaction; transport classification fixture only.

case_reviews.oracle: Closed input gate invokes neither retained-money callback nor step, emits baseline only and leaves next ID at 1.
case_reviews.limits: Pure transport gate boundary with injected None permit.

case_reviews.oracle: Both open and closed input gates avoid any historical bank lookup. Only the open gate calls step; both emit one result after baseline and advance next ID to 2.
case_reviews.limits: This body checks frame count/baseline and invocation counts, not the exact terminal result payload. The adjacent deferred-step case separately decodes a typed refusal.

case_reviews.oracle: A deferred transfer guard invokes no step; generated server frames are fed to the actual client Session, whose step() decodes Rejected status and Rejected disposition.
case_reviews.limits: The client consumes precomputed frames through a second duplex stream, not a concurrently running server or physical network.

consumer_boundary: NPC bank bodies are shared by standalone npc_econ_bank_postgres and registered character_authority_postgres aggregate. No actual compiled ID comparison or duplicate-target removal was performed. Transport cases are included by the dispatch owner tests module.
fixture_boundary: Nine PG cases return Ok when configured_admin is absent. Common Database creates/migrates an isolated local role-controlled DB; Harness seeds Character/session/admission rows using privileged SQL, while node registration, runtime assignment/readiness and subsequent bank/item writes use native APIs. This does not execute fresh Platform admission.

unapplied_observations.fact: The NPC buy test checks one game_item_audit_outbox row per transaction before replay, but its footprint helper does not include that table or NPC trade rows.
unapplied_observations.inference: The replay footprint does not independently prove those event/receipt rows unchanged; this is an oracle boundary, not an executed surviving mutant or a whole-suite gap.
unapplied_observations.recommendation: In a later qualified follow-up, compare the exact relevant event/receipt rows before and after replay if the case is intended to establish a single event across replay.

unapplied_observations.fact: Concurrent drains enforce one Committed and one Replayed via a two-variant enum, but do not compare returned records.
unapplied_observations.inference: The values and row counts prove one money effect, while the exact equality of replayed receipt payloads is untested in this particular concurrency body.
unapplied_observations.recommendation: Retain the case; consider exact record equality in a later qualified change rather than describing count checks as complete receipt equality.
